A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the historical evidence suggests that prizes and rewards were a significant part of the innovation landscape in Britain during this period and that their use was not limited to the eighteenth century, as is sometimes assumed.

prizes and rewards are an important part of a broader policy framework that can help promote innovation, but that they need to be part of a broader package of measures that includes other incentives and supports.

the historical evidence suggests a more mixed and nuanced picture of the use of rewards than is often assumed, and that the historical evidence should be used with caution when drawing conclusions about the efficacy of prizes as a policy tool.

the historical record suggests that the use of prizes and awards was not a panacea for innovation policy.
